title: Charge-selective topological locking and ultraslow coarsening in magnetoelastic media
abstract: We demonstrate that the symmetry of magnetoelastic coupling governs the topological organization of composite defects and can qualitatively alter phase-ordering kinetics. In a two-dimensional theory of an in-plane magnetic vector coupled to elastic strain, we find that integer magnetic vortices bind pairs of elementary elastic half-defects. Isotropic magnetostriction produces a core-induced elastic winding independent of the magnetic charge, giving defect binding without charge locking and leaving the magnetic sector with essentially XY-like coarsening. In contrast, quadrupolar magnetoelastic coupling locks magnetic and elastic defect charges: continuous rotational symmetry favors $q_φ=q_θ$, whereas crystalline anisotropy can reverse the locking to $q_φ=-q_θ$. We reveal that both locking sectors display anomalously slow vortex annihilation: defect density shows a power-law decay $t^{-2/5}$, while the average defect-velocity scales as $t^{-4/5}$. These results are consistent with a dynamic exponent $z\simeq 5$. We show that this coarsening slowdown is associated with large anisotropic elastic friction. An adiabatic elimination of the elastic field reveals that isotropic magnetostriction merely renormalizes local magnetic interactions, whereas orientational coupling induces effective nonlocal interactions between magnetic spins. Our experimentally testable results thus establish magnetoelastic coupling symmetry as a means of controlling defect topology and ordering kinetics.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes defect dynamics in magnetoelastic materials, showing that the symmetry of the magnetoelastic coupling dictates whether defects become topologically locked. Specifically, quadrupolar coupling enforces charge-selective locking and slows down the system's relaxation kinetics to an ultraslow power-law decay, a signature of anisotropic elastic friction.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the symmetry of magnetoelastic coupling dictates the topological organization of defects and fundamentally alters the kinetics of phase ordering in coupled magnetic and elastic media.
main_result: Quadrupolar coupling leads to charge-selective topological locking of defects and results in anomalously slow coarsening kinetics characterized by a power-law decay $t^{-2/5}$ and a dynamic exponent $z \simeq 5$.
method: The study employs continuum magnetoelastic theory, analyzing the free energy functional and deriving effective magnetic Hamiltonians by adiabatically eliminating the elastic field.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D magnetoelastic medium described by coupling an in-plane magnetic order parameter $N(\mathbf{r}, t)$ to an elastic displacement field $u(\mathbf{r}, t)$. The coupling includes isotropic and quadrupolar terms, which govern defect binding and topological constraints.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes purely relaxational dynamics and involves adiabatic elimination of the elastic field, which is valid for certain wave vectors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate defect binding patterns under isotropic coupling and show charge-locking mechanisms under quadrupolar coupling, alongside kinetic results for defect density decay.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the coupled free energy and dynamics, analyzing the effect of different coupling symmetries (isotropic vs. quadrupolar) on defect topology, deriving the effective magnetic energy by integrating out the elastic field, and finally demonstrating the resulting ultraslow coarsening kinetics.
why_interesting: The concept of controlling long-range dynamics (coarsening) through symmetry constraints in coupled order parameters is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in complex quantum materials, bridging statistical mechanics with symmetry principles.
